# Joko Widodo, 2024, 1B.5 Research Note

Assessment: **favorable / effectively not applicable in the coercive sense**. I found no credible 2024 evidence that Widodo used nuclear capability to shield conventional aggression, territorial coercion, or domestic repression. The main reason is structural: Indonesia is a non-nuclear state, and in 2024 it moved further into the anti-nuclear legal architecture.

## Accepted claims

| Valence | Title | Publisher / date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | [Indonesia Joins Global Nuclear Weapons Ban](https://inp.polri.go.id/artikel/indonesia-joins-global-nuclear-weapons-ban) | Indonesian National Police, 2024-09-26 | https://inp.polri.go.id/artikel/indonesia-joins-global-nuclear-weapons-ban | Indonesia formally joined the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons in 2024, which forbids testing, storing, using, or facilitating nuclear weapons. That is direct evidence against using nuclear capability for coercive shield purposes. | `1B.5`, `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.2` |
| Favorable | [Indonesia resmi bergabung dengan negara yang melarang senjata nuklir](https://www.antaranews.com/berita/4357139/indonesia-resmi-bergabung-dengan-negara-yang-melarang-senjata-nuklir) | ANTARA News, 2024-09-25 | https://www.antaranews.com/berita/4357139/indonesia-resmi-bergabung-dengan-negara-yang-melarang-senjata-nuklir | Indonesia deposited its TPNW ratification instrument at the UN on 24 Sep 2024. This is strong evidence that Jokowi’s government was not seeking coercive leverage through nuclear capability. | `1B.5`, `1B.4`, `1B.1` |
| Favorable | [Indonesia | Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons](https://www.icanw.org/indonesia) | ICAN, accessed 2026; treaty status reflects 2024 ratification | https://www.icanw.org/indonesia | ICAN classifies Indonesia as a nuclear-weapon-free state and notes ratification on 24 Sep 2024, with the treaty entering into force for Indonesia on 23 Dec 2024. That background makes nuclear coercion or nuclear shielding in 2024 implausible. | `1B.5`, `1B.4`, `1B.1` |
| Favorable | [Indonesia does not have nuclear, chemical, or biological weapons programs](https://www.nti.org/countries/indonesia/) | NTI, accessed 2026; country status background | https://www.nti.org/countries/indonesia/ | NTI states Indonesia does not have nuclear weapons and has no weapons program. This is background evidence that there was no nuclear capability available to shield aggression or repression in 2024. | `1B.5` |
| Favorable | [Declarations pursuant to Article 2 of the TPNW](https://www.unoda.org/en/our-work/weapons-mass-destruction/nuclear-weapons/treaty-prohibition-nuclear-weapons/declarations-pursuant-article-2-tpnw) | UNODA, accessed 2026; declaration filed 2025-01-21 | https://www.unoda.org/en/our-work/weapons-mass-destruction/nuclear-weapons/treaty-prohibition-nuclear-weapons/declarations-pursuant-article-2-tpnw | Indonesia later declared that it does not own, possess, control, or host nuclear weapons. Although the declaration is from 2025, it confirms the underlying 2024 non-nuclear status relevant to this lens. | `1B.5`, `1B.4` |

## Synthesis

- I found **no evidence on the other side**: no report, statement, or policy showing Jokowi used nuclear capability as cover for territorial coercion, conventional aggression, or domestic repression.
- The 2024 record instead shows the opposite:
  - ratification of the TPNW,
  - formal anti-nuclear legal commitment,
  - and background confirmation that Indonesia has no nuclear weapons program.
- Because Indonesia is non-nuclear, the most defensible reading is that `1B.5` is **not just favorable, but largely structurally inapplicable as a coercive-behavior test** in 2024.

## Search gap

I did not find any reliable 2024 source connecting Jokowi to nuclear-backed coercion. If a later scoring pass wants stricter ruler-level evidence, the limitation is that the record is mostly about **status and treaty posture**, not a direct presidential speech saying “we will not use nuclear capability to shield X,” which would be unusual for a non-nuclear state.
